sources.title: Disclosure is not documentation: an open science framework for documenting generative AI use in scholarly research and publication workflows
sources.scope: Relevant full HTML discussion and the author’s AI-use declaration; supplementary documentation was not fetched.
sources.note: Distinguishes a brief disclosure from documentation of consequential AI use. Its own declared workflow includes author-generated text supported by ChatGPT, Elicit and Grammarly; it should not be represented as a demonstration of the fully embedded workflow proposed here.

sources.title: A systematic map of generative AI guidelines and reporting in ecology and evolutionary biology: towards the framework of AI disclosure for Improved Transparency (AIdIT)
sources.scope: Primary-page metadata and abstract only. Full methods, role definitions, tables and supplements were not inspected.
sources.note: The abstract describes a survey of ecology/evolution journals and proposes AIdIT. Compare its structured approach before claiming novelty or incompatibility. Do not imply that this scaffold independently audited its results.

sources.title: Towards a transparent and reproducible AI-assisted research paper writing
sources.scope: Abstract and relevant HTML discussion of the workflow and transparency report. A linked correction dated 2026-04-17 was visible but not independently inspected.
sources.note: Describes a human-in-the-loop writing process with author-defined perspective and key points. Useful as a transparency-report example, but not evidence that it shares this project’s non-separable conception of reasoning and writing.

sources.title: Leveraging experimental designs in tourism economics research
sources.scope: Primary title metadata and AI-use declaration; not a methodological audit of the whole article. Early online publication in 2025; publisher page identifies the article as 2026.
sources.note: The authors disclose GPT-4o via the API as an initial coding/classification layer for reported study limitations, plus language refinement. Here “coding” means classification, not software development.

sources.title: What Happens When a Black Swan Meets a Gray Rhino? Reflections on the Evaluation Market in Transformative Times
sources.scope: Primary article metadata and AI-use declaration, not a verification of the reported checks.
sources.note: The authors disclose GPT-5.1 for idea generation, writing support, summary drafting and proxy review, and report human verification. This establishes what they declared, not that their checking was independently demonstrated.

sources.title: Responsible and transparent use of AI in scientific publishing
sources.scope: Search metadata only; direct article retrieval failed. Search metadata gave 2026-08-20 as publication date.
sources.note: Retained from the opening discussion as a research lead, not as evidence for substantive policy claims.

sources.title: Spotlight on our AI policies
sources.scope: Title/partial primary-page access; the substantive passage about prompts and coding was not inspected.
sources.note: Do not repeat the opening discussion’s specific claim about mandatory prompt disclosure as verified by this source.

sources.title: Generative AI policies for journals
sources.scope: Relevant author-disclosure, research-use and AI-assisted-coding sections of current HTML. No June 2026 revision date was independently established.
sources.note: Scoped interpretation is in the policy register; do not infer blanket permission for all uses or generalise image rules.

sources.title: AJPS AI Policy: AI Accountability and Transparency Policy for Authors
sources.scope: Author policy HTML, displaying an update date of 2026-08-11.
sources.note: Journal-specific guidance referring to Wiley’s researcher guidelines, not a publisher-wide substitute.

sources.title: Authorship and contributorship: journals
sources.scope: The central AI Contributions to Research Content subsection.

sources.title: Policy and Society: preparing your materials (Cambridge-hosted page)
sources.scope: AI guidance was inspected, but the same page links to Oxford Academic author instructions. Current venue applicability was not resolved.
sources.note: The opening answer relied on this page too broadly. Treat it as a scoped/legacy example, not proof of current instructions for that journal or every Cambridge title.

sources.title: Artificial intelligence: Communications Materials editorial policies
sources.scope: Core expectations and risk categories on the Communications Materials-hosted Nature Portfolio page.
sources.note: The exact target journal and the relevant use category must still be checked.

sources.title: Best Practice Guidelines on Publishing Ethics
sources.scope: Relevant generative-AI and authorship guidance in the general ethics page, not every linked researcher guideline.
sources.note: General ethics guidance does not resolve all journal-specific or task-specific conditions.

sources.note: Keep this retrieval gap explicit; do not silently substitute book guidance or AJPS-specific guidance.
